New learning crowding out old learning is interference (a forgetting path).
Emphasizing a strength to offset a perceived weakness is compensation (covering a weakness by stressing a strength elsewhere).
Denial (refusing to accept an obvious truth) refuses to accept an obvious truth about performance or risk — confront gently with facts and standards.
Repression (pushing unpleasant feelings or memories out of awareness) pushes threatening feelings out of awareness — including a hidden fear of flying that quietly blocks learning.
Unclear objectives and an unprepared instructor produce confusion, disinterest, and lost respect.
Assess against lesson objectives and standards — constructive, specific, and aimed at the next improvement.
Introduce PTS (Practical Test Standards)/ACS (Airman Certification Standards) early and use them as the criterion standard throughout — not a surprise on checkride day.
Interactive/CAL (computer-assisted learning) and commercial prep tools help practice, but they may not match your course objectives — instructor judgment still rules.
Assessment should mirror the objective: knowledge checks for facts, performance checks for skills, and both when both matter.
Authentic / performance assessment fits real-world and critical-thinking skills better than isolated recall items.
Treat anxiety with clear objectives, honest reassurance, and achievable steps — ridicule and surprise standards make it worse.
Integrated instruction starts outside/inside reference early and keeps both in the habit pattern — do not postpone instruments to “later.”
